answer: According to the overview, crises make it easier to dismantle outdated arrangements because they weaken the forces that preserve the status quo and reduce opposition from incumbents, creating a window for governments to act and pursue reforms. The overview says crises “weaken the forces of preservation” and that when they place “intense pressure on governments to act, a window opens for reforms” [wdr-p253-text-001] [wdr-p049-text-001].
